replacements.old: This creates the single biggest risk in the product: an underfunded IUL can collapse. If you pay only the minimum premium, and crediting comes in below what the illustration assumed, rising insurance costs can consume the cash value until the policy lapses — potentially decades in, after you've paid for years, and at an age when replacing coverage is expensive or impossible. Funding an IUL properly is not optional. It is the whole game.
replacements.new: This creates a major risk in the product: an underfunded IUL can lapse. If you pay only the minimum premium, and crediting comes in below what the illustration assumed, rising insurance costs can use up the cash value until the policy lapses. That can happen decades in, after you have paid for years, at an age when new coverage may cost much more or not be available. In a December 3, 2021 consumer alert, Wisconsin’s insurance regulator said it had seen many cases of universal life owners whose policies lapsed with little to no value, or who had to pay large added premiums to keep coverage. Funding an IUL at a level that holds up is the core of the decision.

replacements.old: How to read any IUL illustration: ask for the guaranteed column, not just the illustrated one. The illustrated column assumes a crediting rate that may not happen; the guaranteed column shows what the carrier must deliver in the worst case. If the guaranteed column shows the policy lapsing, you're looking at a policy that depends on optimism to survive. Regulators cap how aggressive these illustrations can be for exactly this reason — but a capped projection is still a projection.
replacements.new: How to read any IUL illustration: ask for the guaranteed column, not just the illustrated one. The illustrated column assumes a crediting rate that may not happen; the guaranteed column shows what the carrier must deliver in the worst case. If the guaranteed column shows the policy lapsing, you're looking at a policy that depends on optimism to survive. State regulators, working through the NAIC, limit how aggressive index illustrations can be (see the NAIC’s life insurance illustrations page), but a limited projection is still a projection.

replacements.new:
Before you buy any IUL: An IUL is life insurance, not an investment in the market. Caps and participation rates limit your interest credits, and the carrier can change them within limits set in the policy. Policy charges come out of the cash value, and the cost of insurance rises with age. Loans and withdrawals reduce the death benefit and can cause a lapse. Surrender charges can apply if you cancel or take money out in the early years. The policy lists these charges, so ask how large they are and how many years they last before you sign. Every guarantee in the policy, including the floor, depends on the claims-paying ability of the insurance company. Illustrated values are projections, not promises. The NAIC’s Life Insurance Buyer’s Guide lists a question to answer from your policy: what part of the premium or policy value isn’t guaranteed?

IUL vs. whole life vs. term

And if you want permanent coverage with guarantees rather than projections, whole life or guaranteed universal life are more honest fits.

replacements.new:
Disclaimer: Honorbrook Insurance is an independent insurance agency. This page is for general educational purposes only and is not insurance, tax, legal, or investment advice, an offer of coverage, or a contract. Product availability, benefits, riders, caps, participation rates, and eligibility vary by state, carrier, and individual circumstances. Read your policy for the terms that apply to you.

Life insurance guarantees depend on the claims-paying ability of the issuing insurance company. Indexed universal life is life insurance, not a security or a direct investment in any index; caps and participation rates can change, and surrender charges can apply in the early years. Illustrations are projections based on assumptions that are not guaranteed. Policy loans and withdrawals reduce the cash value and death benefit, and a policy that lapses with a loan outstanding may create taxable income. Ownership, trust, and estate tax decisions should be made with your attorney and CPA. Coverage is subject to medical and financial underwriting and is not guaranteed to be issued.

Honorbrook Insurance is not connected with or endorsed by any government agency or program.

replacements.old:
Are dividends guaranteed?
No. Dividends are paid at the insurance company's discretion on participating policies and are never guaranteed, even at carriers with long histories of paying them. Any illustration showing dividends is showing a projection. The guaranteed column shows what the carrier must deliver regardless — that's the number to plan around.
replacements.new:

replacements.old:
Is whole life worth it?
It depends on whether you need permanent coverage. If your need is temporary — replacing income while children are home — term life gives far more death benefit per dollar and whole life is an expensive way to solve that. If your need genuinely never ends, or you want guaranteed lifetime coverage plus a predictable asset, it earns its cost. We'll tell you honestly which case you're in.
replacements.new:
Is whole life worth it?
It depends on whether you need permanent coverage. If your need is temporary, such as replacing income while children are home, term life gives more death benefit for each premium dollar, and whole life is an expensive way to solve that. If your need lasts for life, or you want lifetime coverage with contractual guarantees plus predictable cash value, it can earn its cost. We'll tell you honestly which case you're in.
